summary: Emit's report tells a projection it overwrote a hand-edit apart from a plain source-side re-emit, so replaced hand-made bytes are never silent

edit.description: Add the sixth `EmitOutcome` variant (enum line 822, `label` line 856, the per-outcome tally in `render_emit` line 3091) for a projection whose on-disk bytes did not hash to the prior lock's `emit_hash` and was regenerated over anyway: the owned-side sibling of `OrphanDrift`, the discrimination `classify_orphan` (line 2873) already draws off that same column for the ownerless case. `emit` parses the lock once into `lock_doc` (line 1834) and walks `read_prior_provenance_from_doc` (line 2845) for the reap diff (line 1842); build one path-to-`emit_hash` index from that single walk — keyed through `normalize_lock_path` (line 986) against `to_lock_path` (line 976), the join the reap diff already normalizes both sides onto — and hand it to `emit_one` (line 2897, decides at 2993/2999) and `emit_manifest` (line 2124, decides at 2176/2181), the two sites that already read `current` off disk. Classify the new outcome only when a prior row exists AND `sha256_hex(canonicalize_eol(current))` (src/hash.rs:30) differs from it: EOL-blind, so a CRLF checkout stays `Emitted`, and absent a prior row the outcome stays `Emitted` — a first emit, adoption's included (`specs/model/adoption.md`, "Install": the one reviewable adoption diff), overwrites bytes no lock ever fingerprinted on purpose. Emit keeps regenerating whole: no byte of any projection or lock moves, the classification decides the report line alone. Seat the new tally counter so the existing substring assertion at tests/it/emit.rs:1486 stays true, or move that assertion with it.

`a_hand_edited_projection_is_overwritten_not_conflicted` (line 378) asserts `EmitOutcome::Emitted` for exactly this case — its name stays true, its asserted outcome becomes the new variant, and its sibling assertion that the canonical bytes are back is unchanged. Two negative controls already here: `a_changed_payload_field_re_emits_the_projection` (line 355) is the source-side re-emit that must stay `Emitted`, and the `crlf`/`lonecr` pair (line 542) is the EOL case that must stay `Unchanged`. The tally assertions at lines 1099 and 1486 read `render_emit`.

Consumer of the widened enumeration: the projection-tree snapshot prints each entry's outcome via `{:?}` (line 256) off a single emit into a fresh harness with no prior lock, so every row stays `Emitted`. No edit expected.

Consumer of the widened enumeration (line 211): a second emit over an untouched tree, so it stays `Unchanged`; the hand-edit test beside it (line 217) routes through `check`, not emit. No edit expected.
Consumer of the widened enumeration (line 201), same shape as the settings pair — a second emit over an untouched tree. No edit expected.
Consumer of the widened enumeration (lines 362, 384): first emit then idempotent re-emit over an untouched tree. No edit expected.
Consumer of the widened enumeration (lines 438-443, 1252): a first emit and a converging re-run over an untouched tree. No edit expected.

tests.asserts: a hand-edited projection re-emitted reports the new overwrite outcome naming that member, and its tally counter, while the same tree's untouched member stays `Unchanged`; a source-side change still reports `Emitted`; a projection emit never wrote (no prior lock row) still reports `Emitted`; a CRLF-filtered checkout still reports `Unchanged`; `--dry-run` reports the overwrite outcome and writes nothing

acceptance: cargo test green, every other `EmitOutcome` consumer listed in files[] unedited; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` clean (the new variant's doc links resolve).
notes: Routed from the inbox note observed at fca7b4f9, re-verified at HEAD: the report still prints one `emitted` line for both cases. Regenerating is right ("Total, and write-only"); the gap is silence — the reap half already refuses to lose drifted bytes without a finding, and running `emit` before `check` destroys the very fact `root.fresh` would have reported.
